title: Swift Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: print shows a value and ends the line. Text inside quotes is a String.
notes: Keep quotes around a text value.

entries.name: Keep a fixed value
entries.summary: let makes a constant. Its value cannot be changed after it is set.
notes: Use var when a stored value must change later.

entries.name: Change a value
entries.summary: var makes a variable that can change. += adds to its current value.
notes: An Int stores whole numbers, not text.

entries.name: Put a value in text
entries.summary: A backslash followed by parentheses places a value inside a Swift string.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: if checks a Boolean rule, which is either true or false.

example.code:
let score = 8
if score >= 5 { print("Pass") } else { print("Try again") }

notes: Swift if needs a Boolean; a bare number is not a condition.

entries.name: Read an array item
entries.summary: An array keeps values of one type in order. Position zero is first.
notes: An index outside the array stops the program.

entries.name: Walk through a range
notes: 1..<3 leaves out 3; three dots include it.

entries.name: Name reusable steps
entries.summary: A function takes an input and returns a typed result. _ lets callers omit the input label.

example.code:
func twice(_ n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }
print(twice(4))

notes: The returned value must match the declared return type.

entries.name: Choose a fallback
entries.summary: An optional can hold a value or nil. ?? gives a fallback when it is nil.
notes: Avoid force-unwrapping with ! when the value may be nil.

entries.name: Read only when present
entries.summary: if let unwraps an optional only when it contains a value.

example.code:
let score: Int? = 8
if let value = score { print(value) }

notes: The unwrapped value exists only inside its block.

entries.name: Group fields with a struct
entries.summary: A struct groups related values. A Book has a title and a page count.
notes: A let struct value cannot have its stored fields changed.

entries.name: Name a few choices
entries.summary: An enum lists a fixed set of choices. switch handles each possible choice.
notes: A switch over an enum must cover all cases.
